readable-diagrams
Diagrams a reader understands on first look.
One JSON spec → one self-contained HTML page, with a machine-checked comprehension gate.
English | 中文
## Why this exists
Two excellent skills already exist, and they solve different halves of the problem:
| Layer | Comes from | What it gives |
| Validated spec pipeline | Archify (Apache-2.0) | JSON intermediate → deterministic render → gates

|
| Editorial design system | diagram-design (MIT) | paper/ink/accent tokens, type ramp, orthogonal

connectors, accessible SVG |
| **Comprehension contract** | this project | conclusion title, takeawa
y, numbered reading path, legend, caption — **and a checker that fails the page when they are missin
mbered reading path, legend, caption — **and a checker that fails the page when they are missing** |

Neither parent validates that a human can *read* the result. That is the point of
this skill: the pa

ge is not allowed to ship unless the reading furniture is there,
the accent budget holds, contrast c
lears 4.5:1, and the connectors are orthogonal.
## What you get

- **Nine spec-driven types** — architecture, flow, state, sequence, timeline,
tree, layer stack, bar

, quadrant.
- **Chart families by hand** — line, scatter, sankey, radar, heatmap, Gantt, Venn,
funne

l, journey… drawn against the same furniture and the same gates.
- **Two gates, both must pass** — `

self_check.py` (structure, accessibility,
single-file safety) and `comprehension_check.py` (readabil

ity).
- **Hover interaction, no JavaScript** — hovering a node dims the rest and lights
its edges (s

hown above); hovering a reading step lights its node; staggered
entrance; reduced-motion and print f

all back to the static frame.
- **Editorial skins** — light + dark, CJK-aware typography (12px floor

, register
switch for Chinese labels), 4px grid, no shadows.
- **Import / export** — Mermaid, draw.i

o and Excalidraw in; SVG and PNG out.
- **Eight example pages** in `skills/readable-diagrams/example

s/`,
each passing both gates.

A non-zero exit is never success. Failures are ordinary evidence: fix the spec,
regenerate, rerun. G
enerated HTML is never hand-patched.
## Install
| Host | Install |
| **DeepSeek Harness** | Add this repo as a plugin: `dsh plugin --profile desktop add https://github
.com/bingomu/readable-diagrams/archive/refs/tags/v1.1.0.tar.gz` — or the **Plugins → Add** page with

the same URL. Restart the app; the skill appears in the session catalogue. |
| **Claude Code** | `/
plugin marketplace add bingomu/readable-diagrams`, then install `readable-diagrams` — or copy `skill

s/readable-diagrams/` to `~/.claude/skills/`. |
| **Codex** | Copy `skills/readable-diagrams/` to `~

/.codex/skills/`, or point Codex at the repo’s `.codex-plugin/` manifest. |
| **Any agent that reads
`SKILL.md`** | `bash install.sh` (copies the skill folder to `~/.agents/skills/`). |

Every host installs from this repo — no npm package is required. (The DSH in-app
market index only l

ists npm-published plugins, so appearing inside Discover /
dshmarket needs an npm release; direct in

stalls work regardless.) No build step
and no runtime dependencies either: Python 3.9+ for the scrip

ts, Node 20+ only
for the DSH plugin wrapper.
## Examples
| architecture · zones, focal path | flow · a decision hexagon and two routes |
| sequence · who waits on which hop | quadrant · one recommendation, three also-rans |

Open any `skills/readable-diagrams/examples/*.html` in a browser to try the hover
layer.

Run `python3 scripts/check.py` before pushing; it renders every example, runs
both gates, and parses

the plugin entry point. See
CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md.
## License and provenance

MIT. `self_check.py` and the Mermaid / draw.io / Excalidraw extractors are
vendored MIT code from di

agram-design; the design tokens and connector grammar
are adapted from it with attribution. Archify

contributed concepts and the
delivery discipline, not code. Details in
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

Built for the DeepSeek Harness
plugin ecosystem; the skill folder itself is host-agnostic.
